## Why visit

The strongest single match for this trip: a working cask pub in a lavish Victorian interior, with serious cider and a kitchen that makes it sensible to stay for a meal. Look at the glazed walls, decorative ceiling and famously sloping mosaic floor before choosing a Marble beer. This is the brewery’s original home rather than its present production site. Give it a proper sitting; its appeal is the combination of the beer, the room and the food, rather than simply collecting another brewery name.

## Beer

Marble cask is the main draw; CAMRA lists Manchester Bitter and Pint among the regular beers. The official site advertises nine handpulls, while CAMRA describes six cask lines: capacity and actual availability should not be treated as identical.

**CAMRA-listed regular beers:** Marble — Manchester Bitter; Marble — Pint.

**Recently seen or reported (not regulars):** Marble — Stout.

**Named changing/house breweries:** Marble.

*Recheck the dispense and beer clip at the bar. A handpump is not proof that a beer is cask-conditioned; similarly, these beer names do not establish real-cider qualification.*

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA explicitly reports changing real ciders on draught and in bottles; ask what is available and whether any perry is in stock. Central Manchester CAMRA Cider Pub of the Year 2026.

## Food

British pub dishes, including steak-and-stout pie; vegetarian/vegan options and Sunday roasts. Book a meal, particularly Sunday lunch.

## Plan the visit

Opening-hours conflict: the official website currently says Tuesday closed, while CAMRA lists Tuesday opening. Confirm directly before making this a Tuesday anchor. Sunday roasts can sell out.

**Getting there:** Walk from Manchester Victoria or Shudehill; combine with Smithfield Market Tavern and Crown & Kettle.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
